bull_bear.body: Priority on organic greenfield expansion (owned real estate model); Funding mix: Internal accruals + Debt capped at 3x EBITDA; No M&A focus; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but cash flow positive.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory approval delays (Thane expansion, BKC pre-possession); Slower-than-expected ramp-up at Dombivli/Indore; Rupee depreciation increasing capex intensity; Competition in Mumbai/Pune quaternary care.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasis on 'growing right' with owned assets; Prudent leverage management; Transparent on ramp-up timelines (2 years for breakeven).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Company explicitly rejects international medical tourism focus despite government push, citing sufficient local demand and lack of marginal accretion; BKC project positioned as a 'declaration' of premium capability rather than just capacity addition; All pipeline projects are full-scale hubs, not spokes.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Funding philosophy rests on three legs: internal accruals, cash on hand and leverage, under the header "Prudent Capital Deployment to Fuel Growth".
- Internal accruals: "Cash flow to EBITDA conversion averaging ~75-80% over the last five years is expected to support a significant portion of the planned expansion capex".
- Cash on hand: "Cash & Cash Equivalent, including Investments of Rs 537.7 crs".
- Leverage: "Targeted Debt/EBITDA is expected to remain below 3x"; finance cost has increased on account of debt taken for expansion projects.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Thane: 75% occupancy, inflation-led growth; Pune: ~65% occupancy, headroom for volume/mix growth; Indore: 45-50% occupancy (post capacity add), ramping via case mix improvement; Dombivli: 2 months ops, accreditation/insurance pending 6-12 months.

- The newest asset, Dombivli, "completed its first full quarter of operations", with occupancy "increasing steadily, supported by increasing patient footfall, expansion of clinical services and growing patient acceptance".

deepdive.thesis: Jupiter delivered a strong FY26 with 15% revenue growth and 22.9% EBITDA margins, successfully commissioning the Dombivli greenfield ahead of schedule while maintaining a net-cash balance sheet. The key inflection point is the 2-year breakeven guidance for Dombivli and the visibility on funding the massive 1,700-bed expansion pipeline (Pune, Mira Road, BKC) primarily through internal accruals.

open.horizon: by end of 2nd year of operation (~FY28)
open.item: The newly opened Dombivli hospital is expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven by the end of its second year of operations.
Pune South greenfield hospital (500-bed planned capacity, phased) remains on track for calendar year 2028.

Mira Road (Mira–Bhayandar) hospital has completed architectural drawings and is moving through regulatory clearances, with excavation expected before the end of the (calendar) year; expected completion 2029.
A 400-bed quaternary care hospital is planned at Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, expected 2030.
Dombivli, Pune South, Mira Road and BKC together represent approximately 1,700 new beds in this expansion cycle, taking the Company's long-term capacity to nearly 3,000 beds.
Dombivli hospital is designed for phased capacity growth from 200 operational beds (with 300+ beds already fit-out complete) to a total planned capacity of 500 beds as patient demand grows.
An application for amalgamation of wholly-owned subsidiary Medulla Healthcare Private Limited (MHPL) with the Company has been filed before the NCLT, Mumbai, and remains pending regulatory approval.

JLHL intends to expand its healthcare footprint in Western India through additional hospitals over the next few years, aiming to develop a network of multiple hospitals with an aggregate capacity of approximately 3,000 beds.

Following operationalisation of the Dombivli hospital and land acquisitions in South Pune and Mira Road (with BKC land acquisition in progress), the Company expects to exceed its previously stated ~3,000-bed network target in the coming years.
A greenfield hospital at Pune (South), with total planned capacity of 500 beds (Phase I 200-220 beds, Phase II 280-300 beds), is expected in 2028.
A greenfield hospital at Mira-Bhayandar, with total planned capacity of 300 beds (Phase I 150-170 beds, Phase II 130-150 beds), is expected in 2029.
A 400-bed hospital at Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, is expected in 2030; the Company is in the process of acquiring the land for this project.
The Dombivli hospital is designed for phased capacity growth from 200 operational beds (300+ beds already fit-out complete) to a total planned capacity of 500 beds.
